results.title: Baer–Suzuki property for periodic groups at the prime 2
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every group $G$ in which every element has finite order and every element $a \in G$ such that any two conjugates of $a$ generate a finite $2$-subgroup, there is a normal $2$-subgroup of $G$ containing $a$. Here a $2$-subgroup is a subgroup in which every element has order a power of $2$.

results.title: Baer–Suzuki property for binary finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every prime $p$, every group $G$ in which any two elements generate a finite subgroup, and every element $a \in G$ such that any two conjugates of $a$ generate a $p$-subgroup, there is a normal $p$-subgroup of $G$ containing $a$. Here a $p$-subgroup is a subgroup in which every element has order a power of $p$.

results.title: Failure of the Baer–Suzuki theorem for periodic groups at the prime 2

Here a $2$-subgroup is a subgroup in which every element has order a power of $2$.

results.title: Baer–Suzuki theorem for binary finite groups

results.title: The $p$-core of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ and a group $G$, the $p$-core $O_p(G)$ is the supremum, in the lattice of subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ that are $p$-groups, that is, such that every $y \in N$ satisfies $y^{p^k} = 1$ for some $k \ge 0$.

results.title: Baer–Suzuki theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime and $x \in G$. Then $x$ lies in the $p$-core $O_p(G)$ of $G$ if and only if, for every $g \in G$, the subgroup of $G$ generated by $x$ and $g x g^{-1}$ is a $p$-group, that is, every element of it has order a power of $p$.

results.title: Classes of groups
results.caption: Abbreviation

results.title: Hereditary formations of finite soluble groups
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A class $\mathfrak F$ of groups is a hereditary formation of finite soluble groups if every group in $\mathfrak F$ is finite and soluble; $\mathfrak F$ is closed under isomorphisms, under taking subgroups and under taking quotients by normal subgroups; and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $M$ and $N$ such that $G/M$ and $G/N$ lie in $\mathfrak F$, also $G/(M \cap N)$ lies in $\mathfrak F$.

results.title: Saturated classes of groups

results.title: Minimal non-members of a class of groups

results.title: Shmidt groups

results.title: Sapir's group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Sapir's group is the group with presentation $\langle a, b, t \mid a^t = ab, b^t = ba \rangle$, where $a^t = t^{-1} a t$: the quotient of the free group on $a$, $b$, $t$ by the normal subgroup generated by $t^{-1} a t (ab)^{-1}$ and $t^{-1} b t (ba)^{-1}$.

results.title: Extended Cunningham chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ is the sequence $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ of natural numbers given by $e_0 = p$ and $e_k = 2 e_{k-1} + 1$ for $k \ge 1$; in binary, $e_k$ is obtained from $p$ by appending $k$ digits $1$ on the right.

results.title: Initial term of the extended Cunningham chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ has initial term $e_0 = p$.

results.title: Recurrence of the extended Cunningham chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfy $e_{k+1} = 2 e_k + 1$.

results.title: Closed form of the extended Cunningham chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the $k$-th term $e_k$ of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfies $e_k + 1 = 2^k (p + 1)$, that is, $e_k = 2^k (p + 1) - 1$.

results.title: First terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by 2

results.title: Walking to infinity on primes by appending decimal digits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p_0$ there is a sequence of primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ starting at $p_0$ such that for every $i \ge 1$ there are integers $n_i \ge 1$ and $k_i$ with $0 < k_i < 10^{n_i}$ and $p_i = 10^{n_i} p_{i-1} + k_i$; that is, each term is obtained from the previous one by appending $n_i$ decimal digits on the right.

results.title: A power of two minus a much smaller positive number is not a power of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \ge \lceil \log_2 (p + 1) \rceil + 2$. Then $2^k - (p + 1)$ is not a power of $2$: there is no natural number $m$ with $2^k - (p + 1) = 2^m$.

results.title: Extended Cunningham chains generated by primes contain arbitrarily long composite runs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $e_0 = p, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ be the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$. For every $n \ge 1$ there is $i \ge 1$ such that none of $e_i, e_{i+1}, \ldots, e_{i+n-1}$ is prime.

results.title: No binary prime walk to infinity in steps of one or two digits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no sequence of primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ such that for every $i \ge 0$ there are $n \in \{1, 2\}$ and a natural number $k < 2^n$ with $p_{i+1} = 2^n p_i + k$. That is, starting from any prime, one cannot walk to infinity on primes by appending one or two binary digits at a time on the right.

results.title: Counting right-truncatable square-free numbers

When $k = 0$ the range is empty, so $L_{b,0} = 0$.

results.title: Constant curves are not closed geodesics

results.title: Full shift space
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration space of the two-sided full shift on $N$ symbols is the set $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ of all bi-infinite sequences $x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of symbols. It carries the product of the discrete topologies.

results.title: Unit shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unit shift on the full shift on $N$ symbols is the map $\sigma$ from $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ to itself given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, the left translation by one step.

results.title: The unit shift as a homeomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unit shift $\sigma$ of the full shift on $N$ symbols, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, is a homeomorphism of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto itself, with inverse given by $(\sigma^{-1} x)_i = x_{i-1}$.

results.title: Automorphism group of the full shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The automorphism group of the full shift on $N$ symbols is the subgroup of the group of homeomorphisms of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto itself consisting of the homeomorphisms $\varphi$ that commute with the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $\varphi \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ \varphi$.

results.title: One-dimensional cellular automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A map $f$ from the full shift $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself is a one-dimensional cellular automaton if $f$ is continuous and commutes with the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $f \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ f$.

results.title: Jointly periodic points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a map $f$ from the full shift $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself, the jointly periodic points of $f$ are the configurations $x$ that are periodic for $f$ and periodic for the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$: there are $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$ with $f^m(x) = x$ and $\sigma^n(x) = x$.

results.title: Joint periodic count
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Cover count of an element under a family of overlays
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of times the overlays `O` cover the element `i` (equation (1)).

results.title: The n-times coverage function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `n`-times coverage function: the total weight of the elements covered at least `n` times by `O` (equation (2)).

results.title: Submodular set function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set function is submodular if adding an element to a larger set gains at most as much as adding it to a smaller set (the diminishing-returns form, Definition 2 of the paper).

results.title: Monotonicity of the cover count in the overlays
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: More overlays cover every element at least as often.

results.title: Monotonicity of n-times coverage for nonnegative weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonnegative weights the `n`-times coverage function is monotone.

results.title: The `n`-times coverage function is not submodular
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `n`-times coverage function is not submodular (Liu et al., Theorem 1): for every `n ≥ 2`, take `n` overlays that each cover a single element of weight `1` once. Adding the last overlay to the other `n - 1` gains `1`; adding it to `∅` gains `0`.

results.title: Weighted maximum coverage is submodular
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `n = 1` (weighted maximum coverage) and nonnegative weights, the objective is submodular.
